density_g_ml.source: commonly quoted textbook value; check a primary source before citing

boiling_point_c.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Properties_of_water (infobox 99.98 °C) and NIST WebBook https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7732185&Mask=4 (Tboil 373.17 ± 0.04 K = 100.02 °C); rounded to the conventional 100.0 °C, within both (fetched 2026-11-28)

safety.summary: Not hazardous. Hot water can scald.
safety.source: General laboratory safety guidance written for this project; check the supplier's safety data sheet before real use.

display.summary: The most common solvent in the laboratory.

molar_mass_g_mol.source: Sum of IUPAC standard atomic weights for the formula (NIST WebBook lists 18.0153) (fetched 2026-11-28)

enthalpy_vaporization_j_per_g.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Properties_of_water ("40.65 kJ/mol or 2257 kJ/kg at the normal boiling point") (fetched 2026-11-28)

vapor_pressure.source: NIST WebBook https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7732185&Mask=4 (Antoine row 255.9-373 K, Stull 1947, coefficients calculated by NIST); log10(P/bar) = A - B/(T/K + C) (fetched 2026-11-28)
vapor_pressure.note: Reproduces about 3.18 kPa at 25 °C and 99.8 kPa at 100 °C; checked against the same page's value for the normal boiling point.

thermal.notes: Dissolved solutes are not yet modelled as lowering the freezing point or raising the boiling point; the model treats water as pure.
